subject: SS United States
title: SS United States sinking: famous ocean liner is now a Gulf reef
answer: The SS United States, the 990-foot ocean liner that still holds the trans-Atlantic speed record it set in 1952, sank around 9 p.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, about 22 nautical miles off Destin, Florida. Okaloosa County scuttled it on purpose to create the world's largest artificial reef.
in_the_news: The sinking was moved up a day from Nov. 12 because of a high-wind forecast and ran hours behind schedule, drawing large live-stream audiences on Veterans Day.
body:
Crews began flooding the ship at about 1 p.m. It was reported fully flooded by about 4:45 p.m., but it stayed afloat for hours longer; water reached its doors around 8:40 p.m., and the liner slipped under roughly 20 minutes later. It now rests in about 180 feet of water, with its upper decks 50 to 55 feet below the surface. At 990 feet long, it surpasses the 888-foot aircraft carrier USS Oriskany, sunk off Pensacola in 2006, as the largest artificial reef in the world.

The ship entered service in 1952 and on its maiden voyage crossed the Atlantic faster than any passenger liner before or since. It was retired in 1969 and spent nearly three decades tied up in Philadelphia while preservationists searched for a new use. In October 2024, Okaloosa County commissioners voted to buy it for $1 million as part of a $10.1 million project, later increased, paid for with tourist bed-tax money and partner contributions rather than property taxes. The ship spent more than a year in Mobile, Alabama, being cleaned before it was towed out on Nov. 9.

What's next: divers could begin visiting after a 24-hour safety period, and local officials expect red snapper, amberjack and grouper to move in quickly. The upper decks are shallow enough for divers of most skill levels. The ship's two funnels, radar mast and a propeller were removed beforehand for a planned SS United States museum in the Destin-Fort Walton Beach area, being developed by the SS United States Conservancy; no opening date has been announced.

faq.q: Why did they sink the SS United States?
faq.a: Okaloosa County, Florida, bought the ship to turn it into an artificial reef that draws divers and anglers, after years of failed efforts to save it as a floating attraction in Philadelphia.

faq.q: Where was the SS United States sunk?
faq.a: In the Gulf about 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin, Florida, in roughly 180 feet of water.

faq.q: Can you dive the SS United States?
faq.a: Yes. Its upper decks sit about 50 to 55 feet below the surface, within reach of most recreational divers; dives were expected to begin after a 24-hour safety wait.

faq.q: How long did it take to sink?
faq.a: About eight hours. Flooding began around 1 p.m. on Nov. 11, and the ship went under shortly after 9 p.m.
